title: ORCDF: An Oversmoothing-Resistant Cognitive Diagnosis Framework for Student Learning in Online Education Systems

problem.claim: Existing cognitive diagnosis models can learn student mastery levels that are too similar, an oversmoothing issue that may reduce their effectiveness in downstream tasks.

gap.claim: Existing cognitive diagnosis models seldom use exercise response signals during mastery-level learning, using them mainly as labels during mastery assessment.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes ORCDF, an oversmoothing-resistant cognitive diagnosis framework that enhances existing cognitive diagnosis models by using response signals during the learning stage.
ORCDF introduces a response graph that incorporates response signals as edge types and a response-aware graph convolution network that captures those signals.
ORCDF enhances existing cognitive diagnosis models by replacing their input embeddings with the response-aware graph convolution output.

stated_novelty.claim: The response graph is explicitly described as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The abstract reports extensive experiments on real-world datasets, but the reported results are incomplete in the supplied source unit.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cognitive diagnosis models estimate student mastery levels and affect downstream online-education applications.
Existing models are reported to suffer from oversmoothing, with learned mastery levels becoming too similar.
The abstract attributes oversmoothing to limited use of exercise response signals during the learning stage.
ORCDF addresses the issue with a response graph and response-aware graph convolution, using the resulting representations in existing models.
Experiments on real-world datasets are reported, but their conclusions are truncated in the supplied unit.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links oversmoothing to excluding response signals from the mastery-learning stage while retaining them for assessment.

interpretation.claim: Signals used only as assessment labels may be insufficient for learning sufficiently differentiated representations.

application.claim: When learned representations become overly similar, examine whether informative supervision or interaction signals are being withheld from the representation-learning stage.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract does not establish that this diagnosis applies beyond cognitive diagnosis models or online education systems.

unknowns: The reported experimental outcomes are truncated.
The real-world datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not supplied.
The abstract does not provide implementation, training, or reproducibility details.
